quickAnswer: Fuel oil heats 56.6% of occupied homes in Shirley, and 29.2% of all homes date from 1939 or earlier, the 5th-highest share of the 50 towns we serve (ACS 2022). With a median home value of $384,200, the oil-versus-heat-pump question deserves a side-by-side look before a boiler is replaced.
body: ## Old houses, oil tanks and modest home values

The Census Bureau's 2022 American Community Survey (ACS) counts 749 of Shirley's 2,566 housing units (29.2%) as built in 1939 or earlier. Only four of the 50 towns we serve have a bigger share of houses that old, and the middle town's share is 16.6%. Another 218 units (8.5%) date from 1940 to 1959, and 445 (17.3%) from 2000 or later. Only 105 homes, 4.1%, have gone up since 2010, which puts Shirley 44th of 50 on that measure.

The median owner-occupied home is worth $384,200, 48th of 50 for value and well below the $579,150 of the middle town. The median home was built in 1977. With values on the lower side of the group, the installed cost of each replacement option is worth setting out side by side before anyone signs.
## What fills the oil tanks, and what could replace them

Fuel oil or kerosene heats 1,397 occupied homes (56.6%), the 13th-highest share, against 36.5% for the middle town. Utility gas serves 467 homes (18.9%), electricity 418 (16.9%), bottled gas 100 (4.0%) and wood 60 (2.4%). With oil so dominant, a failed boiler often raises one question: another oil boiler, or a heat pump. Neither is automatically right, and the answer depends on the house, its insulation and whether heat travels by radiators or ducts.
Gas is the rarer fuel here, 42nd of 50 for share. Moving to it depends on whether a main runs past the house, and the gas company can answer that where the census cannot.
## Seven cotton mills and a Shaker village

According to Wikipedia, English pioneers first settled Shirley about 1720, and the town separated from Groton and was incorporated in 1753. A paper mill opened around 1790 and the first of seven cotton mills in 1812. Two of the large 19th-century mill buildings have since been subdivided and adapted for use by 21st-century businesses. Shirley Shaker Village was established in 1793 and closed in 1908, and its remains are preserved within the grounds of the state prison.

Buildings from those centuries generally predate modern insulation, so heat loss can differ a lot from one old structure to the next. A converted commercial space is its own calculation rather than a catalog install, so a quote for one should start from the building's heating load, which is the assessment we make before quoting any system.
## Apartment buildings and rental heat

Detached houses dominate, with 1,883 units (73.4%), yet 377 units (14.7%) sit in buildings with 5 or more units. Another 66 are in two-unit buildings and 15 in buildings with 3 or 4. Renters hold 530 households (21.5%), 17th of 50, against 16.4% for the middle town.

For tenants, the heating-season floor under 105 CMR 410.201 is 68 F during the day (7 a.m. to 11 p.m.) and 64 F overnight, and heat is the landlord's bill unless the lease assigns it elsewhere. That is general information, not legal advice. For anyone who owns rental property, a dependable boiler matters most in January.
## National Grid and the rebates

Shirley's electricity comes from National Grid, and the company's Massachusetts Electric Company territory list includes the town. Mass Save's standard heat pump rebates therefore reach customers here, under the conditions set out on the [heat pump page](/cities/shirley/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).

faq.q: Should I replace my Shirley oil boiler with a heat pump?
faq.a: It can. With 56.6% of occupied homes burning oil, a heat pump takes the deliveries out of the picture, and the old boiler can stay on as a cold-snap partner. What suits your house turns on how well it holds heat, and that is what our heating-load assessment, done before we quote a system, measures.

faq.q: Does the age of my Shirley house change the system size I need?
faq.a: Yes. Shirley has two big groups of homes: 749 built before 1940 and 756 built from 1980 to 1999. Insulation and air leakage can differ a lot between them, so the same square footage may call for very different equipment. Correct sizing matters more than brand.

faq.q: What about heating a converted mill or other commercial space?
faq.a: Shirley's history includes seven cotton mills, and two large mill buildings have been adapted for use by 21st-century businesses. We serve businesses as well as homes. A converted building can have ceilings, windows and layouts that differ from a house, which changes the load a new system must carry.

faq.q: What should I do if my boiler fails on a winter night?
faq.a: Phone (508) 786-8755, day or night, because emergency calls are taken around the clock. Oil households can check the tank gauge first, since an empty tank is a quick cause to eliminate. Do not tamper with safety controls; a licensed technician should examine the equipment.

heating-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Oil leads in Shirley, but 100 homes use bottled gas, 60 burn wood and 28 rely on other fuels or coal, so a failed boiler or furnace is rarely a simple like-for-like swap. The fuel and the venting path steer the choice.
body: ## When the fuel is not oil

Oil leads by a wide margin, yet the 2022 ACS also counts 100 Shirley homes on bottled or tank gas, 60 on wood and 28 on other fuels or coal. A bottled-gas home buys fuel by delivery much as an oil home does. A wood-heated home may want a second source for nights when the stove is out. Electricity heats another 418 homes, and Shirley ranks 10th of 50 for electric heat.
### Age narrows the choices

Of Shirley's housing units, 1,365 (53.2%) predate 1980, a little under the 57.2% of the middle town. Older houses tend to leak more air, which can make a heating system look undersized when the envelope is the real culprit. The vent path, whether a masonry chimney, a liner or a sidewall vent, also decides which boiler or furnace models fit.
### Gas permits

Gas work is licensed work. Only licensed plumbers and gas fitters can pull a gas permit in Massachusetts, and a new gas boiler or furnace normally ends with a final inspection. The town's building department can explain how it takes applications.
### Buildings with several units

Shirley counts 458 units (17.8%) in multi-unit buildings. One boiler in such a building can serve several households, so a failure becomes a shared emergency, and a planned swap in late summer is gentler than a breakdown in January.
### Repair or replace

Repair suits a fairly young system with one failed part. Think replacement when the same system keeps failing, when a boiler section leaks or when a heat exchanger has cracked. Compare the repair bill with the remaining life of the equipment, not just with the price of a new one.
Related reading: the [maintenance page](/cities/shirley/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) covers how a yearly visit can reduce the chance of a no-heat call.

faq.q: Can I switch from oil to gas in Shirley?
faq.a: Only where a gas main serves the street or can be extended to it. Utility gas heats 18.9% of Shirley homes and ranks 42nd of 50, so ask the gas company about your address first. Then compare the connection cost, a gas boiler and its permit against a new oil boiler or a heat pump.

faq.q: Why does the age of my house matter for a new boiler?
faq.a: Older houses leak more air and often have heat distribution designed for a different era. In Shirley, 29.2% of homes predate 1940 and 53.2% predate 1980, so the load of your particular house, not its square footage alone, should set the equipment size. A boiler that is too large cycles often and wastes fuel.

faq.q: What does a heat failure in a rental mean for the owner?
faq.a: With 530 renter households in Shirley, a dead boiler in a rental is urgent for the owner as well as the tenants. The state sets minimum indoor temperatures for rented homes in the heating season. Servicing the system early and keeping a replacement plan ready makes a January failure easier to handle.

air-conditioning-installation-repair.quickAnswer: Shirley has 1,883 detached houses, 195 townhouses and 30 mobile homes, and each type cools differently. Good ductwork suits a central system, while ductless mini-splits fit houses that have no usable ducts.
body: ## Cooling different kinds of home

The 2022 ACS puts detached houses at 73.4% of Shirley's housing, a little under the 76.7% of the middle town. Townhouses add 195 homes (7.6%) and mobile homes 30 (1.2%). Space for the outdoor unit is the first constraint: a townhouse may offer only a narrow strip, while a detached lot often has more choices.
### Ducts or no ducts

Many older homes were built before central air was common, and the median Shirley home dates from 1977. A house heated by hot-water radiators or baseboards has no supply ducts to borrow. That is where a mini-split earns its keep: one outdoor unit, a small indoor head in each space, and a thin line set through the wall instead of ductwork in the ceiling.
### The biggest age band

Homes from 1980 to 1999 make up 756 units (29.5%), the largest age band in town. If one of them has forced-air heating, its ducts might serve a central cooling unit once someone checks that they are sized for cooling airflow.
### Apartments and townhouses

In a building with 5 or more units, of which Shirley has 377 homes, tenants and condo owners often need the owner's or association's approval before outdoor equipment goes up. Wall-mounted indoor heads and a compact outdoor unit can be easier to approve than a large central condenser.
### Electric homes

Electricity heats 418 Shirley homes (16.9%). A single heat pump can handle both seasons for them, which turns a cooling purchase into a heating decision as well. The [heat pump page](/cities/shirley/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits) covers the rebate side.
### Sizing and breakdowns

Bigger is not better. A unit that is too large cools fast, stops before it has pulled moisture from the air, and the house can stay clammy. Sizing from the house itself, its insulation and windows, tends to beat a rule of thumb. A weak capacitor or a dirty coil is a modest repair, while a refrigerant leak or a failed compressor on an old unit changes the math.

faq.q: Can I cool a Shirley house that has radiators?
faq.a: Yes. A ductless mini-split needs no ductwork, only a small line set between the outdoor and indoor units. Each indoor head serves one area, so the number of heads depends on which rooms you want cooled and how the house is laid out.

For one room it can be. For several rooms, a mini-split is quieter, keeps the windows free and can also heat in winter. Compare its installed cost with several window units replaced over the years. Estimates are written and free, and they arrive before any work begins.

faq.q: Where should the outdoor unit go?
faq.a: Away from bedroom windows, with clear space around it and above the level where snow drifts or leaves pile up. A townhouse or a tight lot may limit the options, while a detached house on a larger lot may offer more. The exact spot is best settled on site.

heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits.quickAnswer: Shirley has 1,397 oil-heated homes and National Grid as its electric utility. Only 17.3% of homes were built in 2000 or later, so the weatherization test is the step many owners will meet first.
body: ## Heat pumps in a town of oil boilers

Mass Save's 2026 whole-home rebate is $2,650 per ton, up to $8,500 per home, and National Grid customers in Shirley can use it. The home must be sufficiently weatherized first, and the full rules are on our [general heat pump page](/services/heat-pumps-ductless-mini-splits).
### Which houses the weatherization test favors

On the age route, 445 Shirley units (17.3%) were built in 2000 or later, and 105 of those (4.1%) since 2010. At the other end, 1,365 units (53.2%) predate 1980 and 749 of them are from 1939 or earlier. Those older houses are more likely to start with a Home Energy Assessment than to pass on age. Shirley ranks 44th of 50 for homes built since 2010, so the age route will not cover most owners.
### The fuel mix

Oil (1,397 homes), bottled gas (100) and wood (60) all depend on deliveries or on stocking fuel, and a heat pump can replace part or all of that. Utility gas homes (467) compare against a fuel that arrives by pipe, which is a different decision. Electric-heat homes (418) would swap resistance heat for a heat pump, which moves heat instead of making it.
### Keeping a boiler as backup

A hybrid leaves the old boiler or furnace in place for the coldest days while the heat pump handles milder weather. It spreads the risk between two systems, though the old one still needs its own yearly care and its own fuel deliveries.
### Ducted or ductless

In a hot-water-heated house, ductless heads are the usual route because there are no ducts to reuse. In a forced-air house, a ducted unit can reuse sound ductwork. Shirley has 1,883 detached houses and 195 townhouses, and the layout of each decides how many indoor units make sense.
See the [heating page](/cities/shirley/heating-installation-repair) for how a heat pump compares with replacing a boiler.

faq.q: How does my house's age affect a heat pump project in Shirley?
faq.a: Mostly through the weatherization test. Houses from 2000 on clear it by age alone, while the 1,365 units built before 1980 more likely start with an assessment. Air leakage also matters for sizing, since a leaky house loses heat faster than a tight one.

faq.q: Can the oil boiler stay when a heat pump goes in?
faq.a: Yes. That setup leaves the oil boiler as backup and lets the heat pump handle milder weather. The oil burner stays in service, so its yearly cleaning does not disappear. Sizing the heat pump to the house matters more than the brand on its cabinet.

faq.q: Will a heat pump work through a Shirley winter?
faq.a: Cold-climate models are designed for New England winters. How well one performs in a given house depends on sizing, insulation and how heat is distributed. Shirley's 749 pre-1940 houses may need more envelope work than a newer house before a heat pump can carry the load alone.

hvac-maintenance-tune-ups.quickAnswer: Oil heats 1,397 homes in Shirley, so the yearly burner cleaning is the service that applies to the largest group of homes. Gas, bottled-gas, wood and electric systems each have their own checks, and spring belongs to cooling equipment.
body: ## A service calendar for an oil-heavy town

Oil is the biggest group by far. An oil system generally needs a yearly cleaning and tune-up: the burner and boiler or furnace are cleaned, the nozzle and filter are replaced and combustion is tested. Skipping a year can let soot build up and shorten the life of the equipment. Late summer or early fall is the usual window to schedule it.
### Checks by fuel

- **Utility gas, 467 homes:** burner, venting and controls inspected for safe, clean operation.
- **Bottled gas, 100 homes:** the same checks, plus the regulator and the gas piping.
- **Electric and heat pump homes, 418:** clean filters, check the coils, clear the drain and review the refrigerant side.
- **Wood, 60 homes:** any boiler or furnace alongside the stove still needs its own yearly check.
### Rentals and larger buildings
About one Shirley household in five rents. In a larger building one boiler can serve several households, so a visit before the first cold spell protects more people than it would in a single house.
### Empty and part-time properties

The 2022 ACS counts 96 vacant housing units in Shirley (3.7%), against 3.6% for the middle town. Equipment that sits unused can still need a start-up check before the heating season, so an owner who has not run a system in a while should have it looked at first.
### Seasons

- **Late summer to early fall:** heating tune-ups.
- **Spring:** cooling and mini-split checks before the first hot week.
- **Any time:** short cycling, a new smell, soot or a jump in fuel use is a reason to call early.

Between visits, clear leaves and snow from outdoor units and keep storage away from the boiler. The [heating page](/cities/shirley/heating-installation-repair) covers what happens when a repair is no longer worth it.

faq.q: How often should an oil boiler be serviced?
faq.a: Once a year, before the heating season starts. The visit covers cleaning, the nozzle and filter, and a combustion test, and it is usually a smaller job than a no-heat emergency in the middle of winter. A burner left alone for seasons collects soot, and soot on the heat exchanger can make the system burn more fuel for the same warmth.

faq.q: Does a heat pump need maintenance?
faq.a: Yes, though the list is shorter than for a burner: clean filters, clear coils indoors and out, and a condensate drain that runs freely. A yearly refrigerant-side check can catch a slow leak early, before the system struggles in the coldest or hottest weeks. Outdoor units also need space around them, so trim plants and keep snow off the cabinet.

faq.q: What should a landlord service before winter?
faq.a: The boiler or furnace, the thermostats and any circulator or blower, since a failure in a cold snap leaves tenants without heat. Shirley has 530 renter households and 377 homes in buildings with 5 or more units, so one failed boiler can affect many people at once.

indoor-air-quality.quickAnswer: Shirley's housing spans 749 units from 1939 or earlier to 445 from 2000 on. Older houses tend to leak air and newer ones to hold it, and each pattern calls for different attention to ventilation and moisture.
body: ## Air quality across Shirley's age bands
The 2022 ACS sorts the town's housing into 749 units from 1939 or earlier, 218 from 1940 to 1959, 398 from 1960 to 1979 (15.5%), 756 from 1980 to 1999 and 445 from 2000 on.
### Leaky older houses

Gaps in an old frame let stale air out but also let pollen, dust and basement damp in. Old paint, insulation or flooring can contain materials best identified by a qualified specialist before a renovation begins.
### Tighter newer houses

In the 756 units from 1980 to 1999 and the 445 from 2000 on, air tends to stay inside. Cooking fumes, moisture and chemicals from furnishings need a way out, so a range hood that vents outdoors and bath fans that actually run can matter more than they would in a drafty house.
### Combustion and wood
60 Shirley homes list wood as the main fuel and 1,397 burn oil. Any combustion appliance should vent properly, and carbon monoxide alarms are basic safety equipment.
### Water and wetlands

Wikipedia describes Shirley as bounded by the Squannacook and Nashua rivers, with Mulpus Brook, Catecunemaug Brook, Spruce Swamp and Tophet Swamp inside its 15.9 square miles. Water covers 0.50% of the area, but whether a particular basement is damp depends on the house and its drainage, not on the town map. A cheap hygrometer shows whether the problem is real before any equipment is bought.
### Converted mill space

Two of the large 19th-century mill buildings have been subdivided and adapted for 21st-century businesses. A commercial space in a converted building can have its own ventilation needs, and we work on businesses as well as homes.
### Options

- Better filtration, changed on schedule.
- A humidifier or dehumidifier matched to the system.
- Added or repaired ventilation for a tight house.
- Ducts cleaned only when there is a visible reason, with the source of the dirt fixed.
The [maintenance page](/cities/shirley/hvac-maintenance-tune-ups) explains regular filter and coil care.

faq.q: Do I need my ducts cleaned?
faq.a: Only if there is a visible reason, such as dust blowing from registers, mold, or debris after a renovation or a pest problem. Cleaning ducts that are in good shape may not change air quality much. A look inside the ducts comes first, and cleaning follows only if that look finds a reason.

faq.q: Why does my basement smell damp?
faq.a: Moisture can come up from the ground, leak from plumbing or condense when humid air meets cool walls. A dehumidifier treats the air only; if water is entering, the entry point is the real job, and the smell comes back until it is dealt with.

faq.q: Does a tight newer house need a ventilator?
faq.a: Not necessarily, but it can help. A house that holds air needs fresh air from somewhere: bath fans, a range hood and sometimes a dedicated ventilator. Shirley has 756 homes from 1980 to 1999 and 445 from 2000 on, the ones most likely to benefit.
